Commentary of Ibn Juzayy (al-Tashil) on surah 78, verses 1–3:

﴿Concerning what are they asking one another?﴾ The original form of ʿamma is ʿan mā (ʿan + mā). The nūn was assimilated into the mīm, and the alif of mā was deleted because it is an interrogative (istifhāmiyya). Its full form is: ʿan ayyi shay'in yatasāʾalūn (about what thing are they asking one another?). The interrogation here is not meant merely as a question; rather, the intent is to magnify the matter. The pronoun in yatasāʾalūn refers either to the disbelievers of Quraysh, or to all people, meaning that some of them ask others. ﴿About the great news﴾ refers to what the Sharīʿa brought: tawḥīd (divine oneness), resurrection (baʿth), recompense (jazāʾ), and other things. ʿAn al-nabaʾ (about the news) is connected to a verb that is omitted and explained by the apparent verb, its estimated form being: yatasāʾalūn ʿan al-nabaʾ (they ask one another about the news). This sentence serves as an answer to the interrogation and as a clarification of what is being asked about, as if, when He said ʿamma yatasāʾalūn (about what are they asking one another?), He answered, saying yatasāʾalūn ʿan al-nabaʾ al-ʿaẓīm (they ask one another about the great news). It has also been said that ʿan al-nabaʾ is connected to the apparent verb yatasāʾalūn, and the meaning on this view is: about what thing are they asking concerning the great news? The first view is more eloquent and more excellent. Accordingly, it is appropriate to pause at His words ʿamma yatasāʾalūn. ﴿About which they are in disagreement﴾: if the pronoun in yatasāʾalūn refers to the disbelievers of Quraysh, then their disagreement is that some of them definitively assert it to be false, while others are in doubt; some say it is sorcery, some say it is poetry or soothsaying, and other things. If the pronoun refers to all people, then their disagreement is that some of them are believers and others are disbelievers.

It was also said that the meaning is "according to their deeds." ﴿رَّبِّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ﴾: with the nominative (*raf‘*), it is either a subject or the predicate of an implied inceptive; with the genitive (*khafd*), it is an adjective of *Rabbika*. ﴿وَٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ﴾ with the genitive is an adjective, and with the nominative it is the predicate of the subject or the predicate of an implied inceptive. ﴿لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ مِنْهُ خِطَاباً﴾: Ibn ‘Atiyya said the pronoun refers to the disbelievers, meaning they do not have the ability to address Him, neither by way of excuse nor otherwise. It was also said the meaning is that they are unable to be addressed by Him, like His saying: "Allah will not speak to them." al-Zamakhshari said the pronoun refers to all creation, meaning that none of them has in his hands any part of address from Allah. ﴿يَوْمَ يَقُومُ ٱلرُّوحُ﴾: it was said that *al-Rūḥ* is Jibril. It was also said that it is a great angel who alone forms one row, while the angels form another row. It was also said that it means the souls of the children of Adam, so it is a collective noun. *Yawma* is connected to *lā yamlikūn* or to *lā yatakallamūn*. ﴿لاَّ يَتَكَلَّمُونَ﴾: the pronoun refers to the angels and the Spirit, meaning that awe prevents them from speaking except after Allah gives them permission. "And he said what is correct" will occur in that station according to this view. It was also said that the pronoun refers to humankind specifically, and that the correct word referred to is "There is no god but Allah," meaning whoever said it in the world. ﴿ذَلِكَ ٱلْيَوْمُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ means the true day, in the sense that its existence and its occurrence are true. ﴿فَمَن شَآءَ﴾ is a specification and an encouragement. ﴿عَذَاباً قَرِيباً﴾ means the punishment of the Hereafter. It is described as near because everything that is coming is near, or because the world, in its entirety, is near. ﴿يَوْمَ يَنظُرُ ٱلْمَرْءُ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ﴾: *al-Mar’* here is general, including both the believer and the disbeliever. It was said it refers to the believer, and it was said it refers to the disbeliever, but the general meaning is better, because everyone sees what he did, according to His saying, may He be exalted: "So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it" [al-Zalzalah: 7], and the rest of the verse. ﴿وَيَقُولُ ٱلْكَافِرُ يٰلَيْتَنِي كُنتُ تُرَاباً﴾: he wishes that on the Day of Resurrection he were dust, so that he would not be reckoned with or recompensed. It was also said that he wished that in the world he had been dust, meaning that he had not been created. It is narrated that the beasts will be gathered so that retribution may be taken for some of them from others, then they will be returned to dust, so the disbeliever wishes to be dust like them. This strengthens the first view. It was also said that the disbeliever here is Iblis, who wishes that he had been created from dust like Adam and his descendants, when he saw their reward, although he had belittled dust in His saying: "You created me from fire and You created him from clay" [al-A‘raf: 12].
